cells.tense: Right now you're the one holding steady for other people, and it isn't costing you.
cells.ask: Pick one person and give them something concrete — time, a hand with a task, a bit of money. Small and finishable today. Then notice you could afford it.
cells.core:
You give steady, measured help to the people around you, and you know you're doing it. Something near you has ended or is finishing, and instead of going scattered you kept your feet under you and passed what you had to the next person who needed it. Strength moves between you and them, and it isn't grinding you down. You hand over what's needed by measure, keep enough for yourself, and the help lands because you're the one sending it.

This isn't the loud kind. It's the kind people lean on quietly in a month when the plans fell through and the ground shifted. You can't steer much by something this plain, but it's how the next thing gets built: what you hand out already has the shape of what comes after. Give what's actually available, to someone actually there. That's the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: You share what you have by measure, and it holds.
cells.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — strength that moves between people.
cells.place: standing where something has ended and the ground is clearing.

cells.tense: You're already giving to people who haven't asked yet, and bracing for how you'll cover what none of them need.
cells.ask: Hold back one offer of help nobody asked you for. Give it a day. Let them handle it, and don't call to check.
cells.core:
You're pouring out before anyone asks. Somewhere ahead of you, every hole is already covered, and you're living in that — so you push help onto people who haven't asked, prop up endings that are trying to happen, take on loads nobody handed you. Nothing near you gets to finish, because you brace it up before it can fall. What used to be light now carries weight for a room no one else is standing in.

This is the same strength with no stop on it. Holding without forcing is the other face — the kind that contains pressure instead of pouring past it. You don't have to become hard. Set one offer down unfinished, let an ending finish itself, and see what comes back at you: more fairness, or just more space. You can pick the help back up tomorrow if it's still needed. Today, one thing stays theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up endings that were trying to finish on their own.

cells.tense: What you hand out and what comes back has stopped moving between you and anyone.
cells.ask: End one arrangement that's already over — a standing offer you've kept open, a key you still hold. Tell the one person who needs to know, and stop offering it.
cells.core:
The flow of help between you and other people has gone quiet. You keep your reserves to yourself, and here, where something was supposed to end and you haven't quite let it, you hold what you hold and nothing moves — not out to anyone, not on to whatever comes after. That's not coldness. It's a faucet with nothing running through it, and the ground around it drying out.

What finished doesn't need your weight on it anymore. Setting it down is what keeps your strength clean instead of locked. Can you release a thing you've already completed? Close one loop that's over. The next bit of help can go out later, to whoever's actually there to take it.
cells.sheetLine: You gave freely once, and now nothing passes either way.
cells.verb: sharing strength outward by measure — strength that moves between people.

cells.tense: You are already standing steady for people around you, and you call it just how the week is going.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been doing as though it were required. Say out loud that you chose to hold it. Then say which way you're pointing it.
cells.core:
You're the steady one — when something falls apart near you, you move things around and people come to you for it. You keep doing it, and your account of it has the situation doing that. You're steering where your support goes without saying so, which is why certain people end up leaning on you and others get nothing at all. The helping is running. Nobody has named who's driving it.

That matters, because help with no direction drifts wherever whoever shouts first. The older form of this is simple: pick the light you're moving toward, then give by what's actually yours to give. You might say that's just what the week requires. Fair enough. Then decide which direction you're already leaning, and put that part into words once. It'll outlast the week.
cells.sheetLine: The steady hand here is yours, whether or not you say so.

A reader could say that was never theirs to release, so I never claim what was released or who it went to. The asks hold if I'm wrong: holding back one offer still stands, and releasing one thing already finished still stands. Watch the sentence that flatters me: 'the giving is the leverage, not the loss' — that's my instrument, not their day, and it's cut below.
